Corporation'''|DIC株式会社|Dī Ai Shī Kabushiki-gaisha}} is a Japanese chemical company, specializing in the development, manufacture and sale of inks, pigments, polymers, specialty plastics and compounds and biochemicals.{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/finance/stocks/companyProfile?symbol=4631.T |title=Company Profile |publisher=[[Reuters]] |access-date=March 26, 2014}} It was founded in 1908 as Kawamura Ink Manufactory, renamed to Kawamura Kijuro Shoten in 1915, incorporated as Dainippon Printing Ink Manufacturing in 1937 and renamed to Dainippon Ink and Chemicals (DIC) in 1962 before the name was changed to the present name DIC Corporation in 2008 on the occasion of its 100th anniversary.{{cite web|url=http://www.dic-global.com/en/about/history/chronicle.html|title=History of the DIC Corporation|access-date=2014-02-16}} The company slogan "Color & Comfort By Chemistry" suggests that DIC products should deliver color and comfort to daily life. The company operates worldwide (through 176 [[subsidiary]] and [[Affiliate (commerce)|affiliate companies]] in 62 countries) and includes the [[Sun Chemical]] corporation, based in the Americas and Europe. DIC in Japan has 10 plants in Japan, located in Tokyo, Chiba, Hokuriku, Sakai, Kashima, Yokkaichi, Shiga, Komaki, Saitama, and Tatebayashi. The main research laboratory in Japan is located in [[Sakura, Chiba]] cooperating with DIC development centers in China (Qingdao DIC Finechemicals Co., Ltd., Qingdao, China) and the Sun Chemical Group's research laboratories (in USA, Germany and UK).{{cite web|url=http://www.dic-global.com/en/r_and_d/|title=Research and Development of the DIC Corporation|access-date=2014-02-16}} The company is listed on the [[Tokyo Stock Exchange]]. ==History== * 1908 Founded as Kawamura Ink Manufactory * 1937 Incorporated Dainippon Printing Ink Manufacturing * 1950 Listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange * 1962 Merged with Japan Reichhold, changed Company name to Dainippon Ink and Chemicals * 1986 Acquired [[Sun Chemical]]'s Graphic Art Material Dept. * 1987 Acquired Reichhold Chemicals, Inc. * 1999 Acquired [[Total S.A.|Totalfina S.A.]]'s Printing Ink Dept. (Coates) * 2005 Sold Reichhold * 2008 Changed Company name to DIC Corporation * 2009 Established DIC Graphics, joint venture with [[Dai Nippon Printing]] (DNP) integrating DIC's domestic printing ink business and DNP's printing ink business * 2021 Acquired [[BASF]]'s Global Pigments Business, known as BASF Colors & Effects (BCE) ==Business and products== DIC is divided in 3 business units and 6 product divisions === Packaging & Graphic === * '''Printing Material Products Division :''' [[Offset printing|Offset inks]], [[Rotogravure|gravure inks]], [[Flexography|flexo inks]], [[Beverage can printing|metal decorative inks]], [[Security printing|security inks]], [[printing plate]]s, jet inks, news inks * '''Packaging Material Products Division:''' Packaging adhesives, coextruded multilayer films, [[polystyrene]] (hyperbranched, GPPS, [[High impact polystyrene|HIPS]]). === Color & Display === *'''Color Material Products Division:''' pigments for printing inks, pigments for coatings and plastics, pigments for specialty applications, pigments for color filters, pigments for cosmetics and [[health food]]s ([[Spirulina (dietary supplement)|Spirulina]]) * '''Display Material Products Division:''' [[Thin-film-transistor liquid-crystal display|Thin-Film transistor liquid crystal]] (TFT LC), Supertwisted nematic liquid crystal (STN LC) === Functional Product === * '''Performance Material''' '''Products Division''': general polymers ([[Alkyd|alkyd resins]], unsaturated [[polyester resins]], [[plasticizers]], waterborne resins, [[acrylic resins]], [[phenolic resins]]) specialty polymers ([[epoxy resins]], ultraviolet (UV)-curable resins, [[Polyurethane|polyurethane resins]], [[Fluorochemical industry|fluorochemicals]]), [[Metal carboxylate complex|metal carboxylates]], sulphur chemicals, fiber and textile colorants * '''Composite Material Products Division:''' [[polyphenylene sulfide]] (PPS) compounds, interior housing products, industrial [[adhesive tape]]s, [[plastic colorant]]s, high-performance optical materials, Hollow-fiber membranes, medical diagnostics products === DIC Color System Guide === {{See also|ja:DICカラーガイド}} The DIC Color System Guide[http://www.dic-graphics.co.jp/en/products/dcguide/ DIC Digital Color Guide][http://www.dic-global.com/en/whats_dic/scene/diccolorguide/ About the DIC Digital Color Guide apps] is a [[spot color]] system, based on [[Munsell color system|Munsell color theory]].[http://www.theinformedillustrator.com/2012/09/process-versus-spot-color.html The Informed Illustrator: Digital Spot Color Systems] It is common in Japan, and comparable in role to the [[Pantone]] systems. === Manufacturing facilities === The company recently inaugurated an advanced toluene-free plant for liquid ink manufacturing called Optima. This is DIC’s fifth plant in India, located at Sakhya in Bharuch district, Gujarat. The plant is built on an area of 92,500 sq. m, occupying 45,000 sq. m of the plot to cater to a growing demand for Toluene Free/Keyone Free (TF, KF/NTNK) inks in the country. Under phase I, the plant has a capacity of 10,000 Tonnes of TF, KF/NTNK liquid inks in two shifts. DIC India further plans to expand the plant to manufacture value-added and specialty products for the domestic and export markets. The company plans to use the remaining plot area to build plants for different types of products in its operations.{{cite web|url=https://textilevaluechain.in/in-depth-analysis/textile-market-report/corporate-update/gujarat-welcomes-the-opening-of-dic-indias-brand-new-cutting-edge-manufacturing-facility/|title=GUJARAT WELCOMES THE OPENING OF DIC INDIA'S BRAND-NEW, CUTTING-EDGE MANUFACTURING FACILITY|date=24 March 2023 |access-date=2023-03-24}} The new plant is expected to provide employment to over 100 people and boost the company’s access to the Northern and Western markets due to its location at the center of the chemical hub in India. DIC India’s other four plants are located in Uttar Pradesh, Ahmedabad (Gujarat), Kolkata, and Karnataka.{{cite web|url=https://www.printweek.in/news/dic-india-inaugurates-liquid-inks-factory-in-gujarat-57346|title=DIC India inaugurates liquid inks factory in Gujarat|access-date=2023-03-27}} ==Cultural activities== *DIC owns 47.7% of the [[sports club]] chain "Renaissance".{{cite web|url=http://www.s-re.jp/company.html|title=Renaissance Company Information|access-date=2014-02-19}} *In 1990, the company established the [[Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art]] to exhibit artwork collected by the company and its affiliates. The museum is located in a 30-hectare park near to its Central Research Laboratories. According to a DIC management decision, partially attributed to shareholder pressure,{{cite news |last1=Stone |first1=Tim |title=Japanese art museum—home to one of world's only four Rothko rooms—faces closure and collection selloff |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2024/09/03/japanese-art-museumhome-to-one-of-worlds-only-four-rothko-roomsfaces-closure-and-selloff |access-date=4 October 2024 |work=The Art Newspaper - International art news and events |date=3 September 2024}} the museum will close on February 1, 2025.{{cite web|title=Museum closure|date=28 August 2024 |url=https://kawamura-museum.dic.co.jp/news/08-notice/}} ==Gallery== {{Gallery|title=DIC Corporation locations|width=250| File:DIC-newHQ.jpg|New DIC headquarters building in Tokyo| File:DICCentralResearchLaboratories20140217.JPG|DIC Central Research Laboratories in Sakura| File:KawamuraMemorialDICMuseumArt2013.JPG|Kawamura Memorial DIC Museum of Art also in Sakura| }} ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== {{Portal|Japan|Tokyo|Chemistry|Companies}} *[http://www.dic-global.com/en/ Official website] {{in lang|en}} *[https://web.archive.org/web/20140222014357/http://www.dic-global.com/en/about/pdf/dic_about_corporate_2013.pdf DIC Corporation, Corporate Profile] *[http://biz.yahoo.com/ic/42/42388.html Yahoo! DIC Corporation (DIC株式会社, Dī Ai Shī Kabushiki-gaisha) is a Japanese chemical company, specializing in the development, manufacture and sale of inks, pigments, polymers, specialty plastics and compounds and biochemicals.
It was founded in 1908 as Kawamura Ink Manufactory, renamed to Kawamura Kijuro Shoten in 1915, incorporated as Dainippon Printing Ink Manufacturing in 1937 and renamed to Dainippon Ink and Chemicals (DIC) in 1962 before the name was changed to the present name DIC Corporation in 2008 on the occasion of its 100th anniversary. The company slogan "Color & Comfort By Chemistry" suggests that DIC products should deliver color and comfort to daily life.
The company operates worldwide (through 176 subsidiary and affiliate companies in 62 countries) and includes the Sun Chemical corporation, based in the Americas and Europe.
DIC in Japan has 10 plants in Japan, located in Tokyo, Chiba, Hokuriku, Sakai, Kashima, Yokkaichi, Shiga, Komaki, Saitama, and Tatebayashi. The main research laboratory in Japan is located in Sakura, Chiba cooperating with DIC development centers in China (Qingdao DIC Finechemicals Co., Ltd., Qingdao, China) and the Sun Chemical Group's research laboratories (in USA, Germany and UK).
The company is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
